chapters.summary: Committee staff welcomes attendees to the Consumer and Worker Protection committee vote, asks everyone to silence electronics and not approach the dais.
chapters.title: Staff opens committee vote and gives housekeeping instructions

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning, welcome to the committee vote on consumer and worker protection.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, we ask that you please silence all electronics and please do not approach the dais.

chapters.summary: Chair Harvey Epstein opens the Consumer and Worker Protection Committee meeting and announces the committee will be voting on Intro 813A.
chapters.title: Chair Epstein opens committee vote on Intro 813A

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: All right, good morning and welcome to today's Consumer Worker Protection Committee.

chapters.summary: Chair Epstein introduces himself and notes the council members present both in person and on Zoom: Wilson, Hanks, Ossé, Banks, Schulman, Ariola, and Aldebol.
chapters.title: Chair Epstein introduces himself and committee members present

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I'm Harvey Epstein, chair of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I'm joined by my colleagues, Wilson, Hanks and Osei on Zoom, Banks, Shulman, Areola, and Audible.

chapters.summary: Epstein explains that Intro 813A allows DCWP to refuse to renew, suspend, or revoke a tobacco or electronic cigarette retail license when a dealer is found to be illegally selling cannabis.
chapters.title: Chair Epstein explains Intro 813A: DCWP authority to revoke tobacco and e-cig licenses for illegal cannabis sales

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: You know, I'm proud to sponsor this introduction, 813A, which allows DCWP to refuse to renew or suspend or revoke a tobacco or electronics retail license by finding the dealers are legally selling cannabis.

chapters.summary: Epstein discusses the 2019-2020 Albany effort to legalize cannabis through the MRTA and how the illegal market undermines the legal market, making enforcement tools essential.
chapters.title: Chair Epstein on MRTA legalization and the illegal cannabis market undermining legal sellers

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: You know, we worked really hard in Albany in 2019-20 to legalize through the MRTA.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: The illegal market really undermines the legal market and ensuring that if the opportunity of someone's engaging in illegal behavior, we can shut it down.

chapters.summary: Epstein references a June hearing where the committee heard that unlawful cannabis sales remain rampant across the city, and that this bill attempts to address that problem.
chapters.title: Chair Epstein cites June hearing findings on rampant unlawful cannabis sales

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: At a hearing in June, we heard unlawful cannabis sales remain rampant in the city.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: You know, this bill really attempts to reflect that change.

chapters.summary: Epstein shares that in 2025 alone, nearly 4,000 pounds of unlicensed cannabis products were seized, worth over $20 million, underscoring the scale of the illegal market.
chapters.title: Chair Epstein cites 2025 seizure statistics: 4,000 lbs and $20M in unlicensed cannabis

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: 2025 alone, over almost 4,000 pounds of unlicensed products were seized, worth over $20 million.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: This bill hopes to rectify that problem in one small way.

chapters.summary: Epstein thanks his colleagues for attending and asks the committee clerk to call the roll for the vote on Intro 813A.
chapters.title: Chair Epstein thanks colleagues and requests roll call vote

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I want to thank my colleagues for being here.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I ask the clerk to call the roll.

chapters.summary: Committee Clerk Matthew DiStefano calls the roll. Epstein, Brewer, De La Rosa, Hanks, Krishnan, Ossé, Schulman, Banks, Aldebol, Wilson, and Ariola vote, with Banks offering congratulations to the Chair.
chapters.title: Roll call vote on Intro 813A

utterances.speaker: Matthew Distefano
utterances.text: Matthew DiStefano, Committee Clerk, Committee on Consumer and Worker Protection.

utterances.speaker: Matthew Distefano
utterances.text: Roll call vote on proposed intro 813A.

chapters.summary: Clerk announces the vote result: eight in the affirmative, zero in the negative, no abstentions. The item is adopted.
chapters.title: Vote outcome: 8-0, Intro 813A adopted

utterances.speaker: Matthew Distefano
utterances.text: By a vote of eight in the affirmative, zero in the negative, and no abstentions, the item has been adopted.

chapters.summary: Epstein thanks everyone for their patience, notes the committee will hold the vote open for a few minutes in case additional members arrive, and acknowledges members have other hearings and commitments.
chapters.title: Chair Epstein thanks members and holds vote open for late arrivals

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: And we're going to hold it open for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: We're going to hold it open just to see if someone else gets here to vote.

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: I know we all have other hearings and commitments this morning, so thank you, everyone.

chapters.summary: Chair Epstein adjourns the committee hearing after holding the vote open for late-arriving members.
chapters.title: Committee hearing adjourned

utterances.speaker: Harvey D. Epstein
utterances.text: This committee hearing is now adjourned.

summary: The Committee on Consumer and Worker Protection, chaired by Harvey Epstein, held a vote on Intro 813A, which grants DCWP authority to refuse, suspend, or revoke tobacco and e-cigarette retail licenses for dealers found illegally selling cannabis.
Chair Epstein cited the MRTA legalization effort, a June hearing on rampant unlawful cannabis sales, and 2025 seizure data (4,000 lbs, $20M) as context for the bill.
The committee passed Intro 813A by a vote of 8-0 with no abstentions, and the hearing was adjourned after holding the vote open briefly for late-arriving members.
title: Committee on Consumer and Worker Protection
topic: Refusing renew, suspending, or revoking a license of a tobacco retail dealer or an electronic cigarette retail dealer that has violated certain authorization requirements of the cannabis law
